chunks: From him, from Ja'far, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who sold a sale that he did not possess until a specified term, and guaranteed the sale, he said: 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no objection to it/is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell a commodity you do not currently possess if you guarantee it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the sale of *al-madmun* (guaranteed goods), a key concept in Shia commercial jurisprudence where the seller guarantees the delivery of a specific item even if not yet in possession. Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling of 'no harm' (*la ba'sa bihi*) establishes permissibility for deferred payment contracts, distinguishing it from *bai' al-kali'* (sale of debt for debt) by ensuring the underlying asset is tangible and guaranteed. This principle facilitates trade flexibility while maintaining contractual integrity under Shia fiqh.
